cases.purpose: Two synchronized writers must see lock contention and preserve the database.
cases.oracle: Independent Python sqlite3 control verifies numeric SQLITE_BUSY with two connections and successful writing after release; candidate uses two separate owned processes on a separate seeded database. SQLite integer row and integrity expectations are literal.
cases.comparison: A holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE and an inserted row at a file barrier until B returns. Both process status files, B stderr, the control result, and independent post-rollback SQLite integrity and rows are retained in HOME diagnostics. Candidate API reports shell status plus diagnostic, not numeric SQLite result codes. A missing barrier, failed control, premature process exit or missing outcome is incomplete, never evidence of a PASS. Busy case checks the diagnostic and final data; no-lock case checks two successful BEGIN IMMEDIATE calls. Raw results require primary review. Busy uses --locking and verifies a committed candidate write after release; no-lock uses the original default.
